name: Infobeans Technologies Ltd
title: Infobeans Technologies Ltd - 543644 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Services-led IT firm with no capacity or pricing disclosure; management gave no guidance, revenue ~539 cr and PAT ~87 cr with AI-led delivery at 43% and receivables rising.

triggers.label: No numeric guidance given
triggers.quote: unfortunately, we do not give any guidance

red_flags.label: Receivables rising; mgmt says 90-day payment cycles

summary.headline: Infobeans Q4 FY26 revenue crossed ₹539 crore (up 37% YoY) and PAT rose 104% to ₹87 crore, with no formal guidance given.
summary.overview: Management reported its first quarter above ₹500 crore revenue and said EBITDA crossed ₹100 crore, with PAT of ₹87 crore. Full-year FY26 revenue reached ₹1,380 million-equivalent growth of 32% YoY (stated as crossing ₹400 crore run-rate breakout), with PAT up 128%. Management stressed a 94% repeat revenue share and a 24% EBITDA margin and 14% PAT margin as the target they aim to hold. Management declined to give guidance, and the call focused on AI product launches (Insane SDD 2.0, RAI agent), the Indore campus investment, promoter stake matters and capital return.

financial_highlights.change: up 37% YoY; USD terms up 27% YoY

financial_highlights.value: Crossed ₹100 crore (first time), margin around 20% to 26% range cited

financial_highlights.change: PAT up 128% YoY; FY revenue crossed ₹400 crore breakout as stated

financial_highlights.value: ₹1 per share regular (₹0.50 normal + ₹0.50 special) for FY26
financial_highlights.change: Four times prior payout; ₹0.25 paid earlier after bonus adjustment

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: US contributed 53% of total revenue, Europe 35%, Middle East (UAE) 7%, and India/APAC/rest of world 4%. Management said Germany grew fastest, US growth was steady, and Middle East grew despite the war situation.

segments.name: Client base
segments.commentary: 18 Fortune 500 clients; 24 new clients onboarded in the quarter; top 5 clients contribute 40% and top 10 contribute 57% of revenue. 11 clients are $1–10 billion enterprises.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it does not provide guidance.
Management said it aims to maintain a 24% EBITDA margin and 14% PAT margin, and will invest in the business, so margins may not expand further.
Target of moving AI-led delivery from 43% of revenue to 100% within 12 months, per management.
Dividend policy set at ₹1 per share regular for the year.
capex_capacity: Headcount at 1,790; management said the recent ~200 addition reflects fulfilment of demand, not anticipation.

Indore campus: company acquired land from the MP government at nominal cost; management said it needs 30–40% of the campus and plans to lease the remaining 60%; rent recovery payback stated at about nine years versus owning.
Buyback and bonus announced in recent quarters; share capital increased to ₹9.7 crore after bonus issue.
demand_pricing: AI-led engineering: 43% of FY26 revenue was generated through AI-augmented work; more than 50% of workforce now works on AI methodologies and tools.
Launched Insane SDD 2.0 (spec-driven development framework) and RAI agent (built natively on MCP, works with multiple LLMs); management says SDD can cut enterprise-grade code time by about 10x.
Management said the Headless offering is a new tool that some clients have started adopting; it expects new opportunities.
Receivables rose by ₹22 crore; management attributed it to longer 90-day Fortune 500 payment cycles and said provisions are held in advance.

qa_highlights.question: How did FY26 growth split between existing and new clients, and what is the new-client contract profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new clients start with small contracts that grow over time; sales team has a two-year earnout. It cited 94% repeat revenue as a sign of relationship strength.

qa_highlights.question: Does the in-house SDD tool compete with or help against client-side LLM tools?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SDD speeds delivery for clients using AI tools, with the AI layer designed to make outputs reliable; it did not compare it with client-owned tools.

qa_highlights.question: Will Infobeans give guidance or geography-wise outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. Management said all geographies are growing and that Germany grew fastest, US steady, Middle East growing despite the war.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 43% to 100% AI-led revenue target a strategy or a product-led change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a multi-pronged, in-house strategy over 12–18 months to enable teams and speed delivery; it said 43% already shows the 100% target is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the promoter gift to a charitable trust made in cash and are further promoter dilutions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gift avoided capital gains tax burden for the company, with the recipient able to draw it over time. Promoters made a public statement in October to dilute or pledge up to 3%; about 0.5% sold so far, with window open until October 26.

qa_highlights.question: What was the currency hedging policy and impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Company previously hedged about 50% of exposure, stopped and restarted several times; no hedging policy in place since January 2026. Management could not quantify currency tailwind or headwind.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: management is investing in the business and the 24% EBITDA / 14% PAT margin target may not hold.
Receivables up ₹22 crore with 90-day payment cycles at Fortune 500 clients; monitor DSO and provisioning.
Concentration: top 5 clients 40% of revenue, top 10 at 57%.
Unhedged currency exposure after stopping hedging in January 2026; FX impact not quantified.
Competitive pressure from clients' own AI and low-code tools (e.g., platform-native agents) raised by analysts; management did not directly address it.
Promoter stake dilution or pledge of up to 3%; window open till October 26.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and AI product launches, but cautious and non-committal on forward numbers: management declined guidance and repeatedly framed margins as targets to maintain rather than expand.
key_quotes: we do not give any guidance

adds.what: Indore campus: land acquired from MP government at nominal cost; company needs 30-40% of campus, plans to lease remaining 60%

growth.why: Management gave no formal guidance and said it does not provide any; it aims to hold a 24% EBITDA margin and 14% PAT margin, with headcount growth (~200 added to 1,790) tied to fulfilling existing demand rather than anticipated capacity, so forward growth is unquantified.
